reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Nehemiah's itemized totals as the more accurate figures, treating Ezra's higher gold and silver totals as copying and rounding errors.

discrepancy.note: Paine's finding that the rosters diverge in their particulars applies equally to the treasury entry, where gold, silver, and garment totals disagree.

quotes.text: Nehemiah, in like manner, gives a list of the returned families, and of the number of each family. He begins as in Ezra, by saying (vii. 8): "The children of Parosh, two thousand three hundred and seventy-two;" and so on through all the families. (The list differs in several of the particulars from that of Ezra.)
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Ezra 2:69 and Nehemiah 7:72.

sides.snippet: they gave after their ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests' garments.
sides.verseText: they gave after their ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests' garments.

sides.snippet: That which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand darics of gold, and two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests' garments.
